correctness.rationale: Every field-linear derivation of a height-two incidence algebra is uniquely (x_e,lambda_e) per Hasse edge. The image lies in the radical and its rank is |{lambda_e != 0}| + r_G({lambda_e=0,x_e!=0}), by projecting onto the complement of the diagonal block and reducing a weighted oriented incidence matrix. Counting the three edge states gives formula (1) and q^(2m) normalization. In the difference from the forest binomial spectrum, minimal cyclic subsets occur first at rank g-1 and are exactly g-cycles, yielding the first-coefficient theorem. Unicyclic formula follows by summing tree attachments. All signs work in characteristic two. Direct enumeration of Leibniz linear constraints in eight finite cases corroborates, but does not replace, the proof.

originality.rationale: Material from general derivation-structure papers (arXiv:2305.02984 and arXiv:2307.08439) and the later journal version provides parameter decompositions and cohomological dimensions but does not state a complete rank distribution for ALL derivations or the girth-reading first coefficient. The nearby element-centralizer/inner-derivation rank enumerator only counts the inner subspace: for a four-cycle over F_2 its normalized histogram is (1,4,30,53,40), versus (1,12,54,109,80) for all derivations. The forest case is subsumed by the known inner count and is not offered as an independent novelty. Full priority remains subject to synonymous terminology and unindexed work.
residual_risks: An equivalent all-derivation operator-rank enumeration may be named as a Tutte specialization, matroid support enumerator, or incidence-algebra differential-operator rank law.
The 2024 journal version was only partially read; any unobserved rank-refinement theorem there would require re-evaluation.
Search ranking/coverage cannot certify uniqueness or exhaustive publication priority.

value.rationale: The rank of a derivation as a linear operator is a canonical statistic of a finite algebra and is finer than the known dimension of its derivation module and the number of inner derivations. The exact general Tutte specialization and the first-cycle coefficient recover girth and shortest-cycle count from one algebraic rank histogram. This is a natural structurally motivated classification for every height-two incidence poset, not an arbitrary small-case census. The known forest boundary is explicitly not sold as a new independent result.
